overview: Chipotle grew Q2 2026 revenue 9.3% to $3.3B on a 2.2% comp, including a 1% transaction gain, while restaurant-level margin fell 220bp to 25.2% and adjusted EPS was flat at $0.33. Adam Rymer, CFO, raised the full-year comp guide to low single digits but guided Q3 to about +1%, assuming a ~200bp Cyclospora-related softening that began in late July continues.
keyTakeaways: Rymer said comps softened about 200bp in the second half of July amid the industry Cyclospora issue, which Scott Boatwright, CEO, said hits sales though Chipotle is not involved.
Rymer expects pricing and inflation to match from Q4 after a first half with pricing near 1% against low-to-mid 3% inflation.
Boatwright said younger and lower-income cohorts improved most and Q2 delivered the highest YoY wallet share gains since 2024.
Digital sales reached $1.3B, or 38.3% of sales, up from 35.5%, which Boatwright tied to the rewards relaunch and Summer of Extras.
financialHighlights: Revenue rose 9.3% to $3.3B, with comps of +2.2% on about 1.6% menu price and +1% transactions.
Restaurant-level margin fell 220bp to 25.2%, with cost of sales up about 80bp to 29.7% on beef, freight and higher usage.
Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.33, flat YoY, and non-GAAP G&A was $176M.
Chipotle repurchased $631M of stock at an average $32.55, added $1.3B of authorization and ended with $800M of cash and no debt.
guidance: Adam Rymer, CFO, raised FY2026 comp guidance to low single digits and guided Q3 to about +1%, or roughly 3% underlying before the Cyclospora headwind.
Rymer expects Q3 menu price in the mid 2% range, with the full year near the high end of 1%-2%.
Rymer guided Q3 cost of sales just under 30%, labor in the mid 25% range, other operating costs mid 15% and non-GAAP G&A around $180M.
Scott Boatwright, CEO, expects about 350 openings in 2026, HEAP in about 2,000 restaurants by year-end and a national catering launch in 2027.

qa.question: What underlies the low-single-digit comp guide, including Q3 to date?
qa.answer: Rymer said traffic improved into early July before a ~200bp softening in late July tied to the Cyclospora issue, and Q3, the toughest lap, is expected at about +1% if that impact continues.

qa.question: Does the ~1% Q3 guide imply ~3% underlying, and where is Max 15 throughput?
qa.answer: Rymer confirmed it, said the duration is very difficult to predict, and put Max 15 at low 20s in-store, mid-teens digital and low-to-mid 30s combined, with HEAP stores two or three entrees higher.

qa.question: What is the margin outlook beyond Q3 as the price-inflation gap narrows?
qa.answer: Rymer said Q3 inflation should be about 3% against mid-2% pricing, and from Q4 the two should match.

qa.question: Why is 350 company openings a year right versus the prior 400 ceiling?
qa.answer: Boatwright said going beyond 350 risks diminishing returns, and extra growth will come from Western Europe and partners, noting Alshaya has 15 restaurants with acceleration in 2027.

unanswered.question: The capex, sales uplift and timeline of refreshing 1,000-1,500 stores.
unanswered.how: Scott Boatwright, CEO, gave a $100,000-$300,000 test cost but said he has "nothing to report today."

unanswered.question: How much LTOs contribute to frequency and traffic.
unanswered.how: Adam Rymer, CFO, said specific LTO lifts are not disclosed, citing only "hundreds of basis points" of typical lift.

unanswered.question: What gives confidence that momentum builds into 2027 despite tough comparisons.
unanswered.how: Scott Boatwright, CEO, cited "green shoots" across initiatives without figures.

risksMentioned: Adam Rymer, CFO, said the ~200bp Cyclospora-related softening may continue through Q3 and its duration is hard to predict.
Rymer said Q3 is the toughest comparison of the year.
Rymer said Q3 inflation of about 3% still exceeds mid-2% pricing, after beef and freight drove cost of sales up about 80bp in Q2.
Scott Boatwright, CEO, said repeat LTOs likely hit diminishing returns around the fifth or sixth run.
